Category: Walkers, Rollators & Accessories > Rolling Walkers

## Features
STYLISH ROLLATOR, EURO STYLE. Easy to use side folding design, a great walker for seniors with sophisticated design and styling. A premium stand up walker for the elderly that won't disappoint in functionality, style, and durability.; HEIGHT ADJUSTABLE rollator walker with seat. The Crosstour walker fits virtually every adult height and is a leader in premium adult walkers for seniors.Locking brakes for use when seating; ROLLATOR WALKER WITH seat 8 inch wheels. The walker has large 8" front wheels for superior maneuverability and is a great walker for the elderly who want their independence but still needing a wheeled walker.; VERY DURABLE, LIGHTWEIGHT, 300LB CAPACITY. Carex mobility walkers are built with durability in mind. Our CrossTour rolling walker with wheels has a 300 lb. weight capacity, built with lightweight aluminum, and can be used on cement and grass.; WALKERS FOR SENIORS SPECIALISTS. Carex knows how to build walkers for elderly. As a medical walker specialist, Carex employees a customer first approach when we build a four wheel walker. Rest easy know our walkers are built for durability.

## Specifications
Product Dimensions: 25.06 x 21.06 x 7.87 inches; 14 Pounds; Department: mens womens; Date First Available: September 13, 2013

## Pricing & Reviews
Price: 90.63 USD.
Rated 4.4 from 706 reviews.
Top review: Five stars for the rollator itself, one star for what I received...I purchased this particular rolling walker to give me more ability to move around outside in the presence of severe orthostatic hypotension. I need to be able to sit down immediately when hit by the "woozies"...The unit is ideal for me. It is robust, lightweight (14 lb), and folds easily (simply by lifting by the handle embedded in the seat) and fits nicely in the trunk of my car. There is an automatic latch to hold the frame open while in use. Although there are many plastic parts they seem to be strong and well designed.I like the "European" style rollators over the standard form.Now for the negatives:1) My summary is that this the best rollator with the worst assembly instructions!I am a retired mechanical engineer and consider myself to be very adept at putting things together, but I struggled with this one! All you get is a single sheet with small photos on it. As an example, these photos do not unambiguously indicate how the rear wheels should be slid in to the main frame - you can do it with the wheels on the inside or the outside of the frame - they fit equally well either way. I, of course did it the wrong way, it all looked good - it rolled around beautifully on a flat floor, but as soon as I took it outdoors on a brick pathway it was obvious something was wrong and the tabs holding the rear reflectors were rubbing on the ground! It took about 20 minutes of watching videos and looking at promotional photos to realize that the rear wheels MUST be installed on the outside of the frame. This is not shown anywhere or mentioned in the assembly photos.2) This one is inexcusable: The unit was shipped double-boxed. As soon as I saw the inner box it was immediately obvious that it had been opened previously and crudely retaped. When I opened it, I found torn up bubble wrap, some parts still wrapped others not. The front wheels had been inserted into the rear of the frame! It was a mess.My conclusion was that I had been shipped a returned unit that was resold as a new one. I don't know where the blame lies, Amazon or Carex. Normally I would have returned it to Amazon as soon as I saw this, but I had an important medical appointment the next morning that involved a long walk an needed the walker to get there... And so I put it together.

results.title: Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker Review: European Design + Great Performance
results.text:
Skip to content

SeniorsMobility is reader-supported. When you buy through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Learn more

 By kbeveridge

Euro-style rolling walkers can be an excellent versatile option because they navigate a variety of surfaces. However, there are so many different models that you may be wondering where to start. Carex offers an excellent product in its Crosstour Rolling Walker model.

The Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker** has a European design that prioritizes functionality and comfort. It performs well inside and outside and is lightweight and portable. However, it has limited storage when compared to other models and can be challenging to put together.**

In this review guide, we take an in-depth look at the Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker. We consider the pros and cons of the rollator, as well as its suitability and intended use. Lastly, we compare the roller to a competing model and help you decide if this is your best option.

Review of: Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker

Please click image for more info

What We Like:

- European design
- Higher weight limit
- Indoor & Outdoor use
- Lightweight & foldable
- Mid-range price

What We Don’t Like:

- Smaller storage area
- Limited assembly instructions

Our Conclusion: The Carex Crosstour Rolling walker could be an excellent option if you are looking for mobility and balance. It is also portable and easy to use outside. Carex is a highly reputable brand, and the Crosstour Rolling Walker lives up to the reputation.

## **Specifications of the ** Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker

- Color: Black
- Material: Aluminium
- Weight: 14 pounds (6.4kg)
- Package dimensions: 29 x 34 x 38 inches (73.7 x 86.4 x 96.5cm)
- Height range: Up to 6’4” (1.93m)
- Maximum load: ** **300 pounds (136.1kg)
- Number of wheels: 4
- Wheel size: 6 inches (15.2cm) back, 8 inches (20.3cm) front

## **Pros & Cons of the ** Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker

The Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker has its pros and cons. Here are all of the factors you should consider:

PROS

- The European design is functional and attractive.
- The rollator can support a higher weight limit of 300 pounds (136.1kg).
- You can change the height of the walker to suit your body.
- It uses two sizes of wheels to navigate indoor and outdoor terrains.
- The walker is lightweight and foldable.
- The wheel design allows you to turn tight corners and maneuver in all spaces.
- It has a mid-range price.
- The seat is wider than average.
- The handles have brakes and an ergonomic grip.
- It includes a storage pouch.
- The backrest is supportive and removable.

CONS

- The storage area is smaller than other models.
- The assembly instructions are limited.
- The seat lacks some padding.
- The storage pouch can fall off when you fold the rollator for storage.

## Features of the Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker

### Comfort

The Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker features a 19-inch (48.3cm) wide seat broader than average. This feature could make it more comfortable for people with wider hips. However, it lacks the comfortable padding of other Carex walkers.

It also has ergonomic grips on the handles. This feature is essential to reduce strain on the wrists and avoid problems like carpal tunnel. Poorly-fitting rollators can cause  long-term problems to the wrists and arms, so this design feature is a big bonus.

### Safety Features

The rollator offers the standard hand brakes underneath the handles. You can use them to slow the walker and lock it into position while seated. In this way, you avoid the rolling walker from continuing its journey and possibly making you fall.

### Durability

The walker frame is lightweight but durable aluminum that can support up to 300 pounds (136.1kg). While not quite a bariatric rollator, it can hold 50 pounds (22.7kg) more than standard walkers at this price range.

Its wheels use soft-grip tires that can maneuver various surfaces without damaging the material. Overall, the Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker is well-built and probably durable enough to justify the price.

### Adjustability

You can change the height of the handles to fit your measurements. The frame has various holes that you can move the handles up or down and fix the position. It can accommodate heights up to 6’4” (1.93m), so it could be a viable option if you are a tall person.

Despite its simple adjustability, the walker can be difficult to assemble. The assembly instructions are minimal, and some of the pieces are not well marked. Therefore, novices may struggle at first.

### Versatility

Versatility is a vital strength of the Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker. It has a design with large front wheels and smaller back wheels, which increases the turning circle and maneuverability. Despite this width, it fits reasonably well in small spaces and allows excellent mobility.

The rollator is also suitable for outdoor use. The large and durable wheels can handle any terrain from grass to smooth concrete. Therefore, you can quickly transition between different locations and environments.

### Portability

The rollator weighs just 14 pounds (6.4kg) and is also foldable. If you need to travel a lot by car, bus, or plane, it could be suitable for its portability. The walker also stands while folded, allowing you to move it through narrow spaces.

### Extra Features

The Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker has a storage pouch that attaches to the frame. The bag is thin but can fit your valuables and some shopping. However, it does not have the depth and amount of space as other Carex models.

## Video Overview of Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker

## Who Should Buy the Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker?

### People Who Need Balance and Support

The Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker uses 4 wheels and a stable frame. It allows you to support your body while you move and gain greater independence. Using this rollator could also improve your balance in the long-run.

It has an excellent turning circle and allows you to maneuver around corners and in narrow passageways. By using the walker, you can reduce the risk of falling and increase your confidence.

If you fit the walker to your dimensions, it can also help to improve your posture. However, make sure that you raise the handles to the correct height for your body. Otherwise, you risk leaning forwards and causing postural problems.

### People Who Visit Many Different Places

The Carex rollator is very lightweight and easy to transport with its folding design. Its wheels are also suited to outdoor terrains like grass, dirt, or small gravel. If you like to travel to and walk around different places, it could be an excellent option for you.

### People With a Reasonable Level of Fitness

Because the rollator’s seat is not that comfortable, it is not the best option for taking rests. Therefore, the rolling walker is better suited to people with a higher fitness level that need fewer breaks.

As a bonus, regularly using a rollator can also improve your aerobic fitness. Therefore, it improves your health and reduces the risk of health complications.

## Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker Vs. Drive Medical Nitro DLX

 

The Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker and the Drive Medical Nitro DLX are two of the most popular European-style rollators. Let’s evaluate the two products and see how they compare:

- Comfort: The Drive Medical Nitro DLX has significantly more padding on its seat. It has an adjustable backrest and a better option if you need to sit frequently or for extended periods. Both models feature ergonomic grips on the handles.
- Safety features: Both walkers have standard hand brakes that you pull up to slow the walker and push all the way down to lock it into position.
- Durability: Each rollator is strong enough to support 300 pounds (136.1kg). They also have a similar frame design and level of durability.
- Adjustability: The Drive Medical rollator is a bit easier to adjust because of its push-button system. It also has an additional 2 inches (5.1cm) of potential height, making it an excellent option for tall people.
- Versatility: Both rollators work well inside and outside. However, the Drive Medical rollator has more extensive, 10-inch (25.4cm) wheels, making it better suited to uneven surfaces.
- Portability: The Drive Medical walker is significantly heavier at 22 pounds (10kg). While it is also foldable, this extra weight makes it a less portable option than the Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker.
- Extra features: The Drive Medical Nitro DLX has a larger storage bag attached to the walker. It could be a better choice if you need to transport more items.
- Price: The Drive Medical Walker is a bit more expensive than the Carex option. Its price is at the high end of mid-range, so it is more of a financial investment.

The Verdict

The Drive Medical Nitro DLX is more expensive. However, it is also more comfortable, adjustable, and better suited to outside terrains.

In contrast, the Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker is more portable and affordable.

## Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker Review Conclusion

In conclusion, the Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker is an attractive and versatile rollator that you can use in many different situations. It is lightweight but durable and rolls smoothly, even over bumpy surfaces.

However, the rollator can be challenging to put together. It also lacks the same amount of storage and comfortable seat padding that other walkers have. Therefore, it may not be the right option if you prioritize comfort and storage.

Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker (Click image for more info)

Compared to the  Drive Medical Nitro DLX, the Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker is more affordable and portable. However, it lacks the same versatility, adjustability, and comfort as the more expensive model.

The height is adjustable, and the sleek side-folding design provides for easy transport and storage. It comes with a bonus cane holder and a large storage bag with a carrying strap that can be removed. A classic looking euro rollator. Stand out from the crowd with the classic feel and look of the euro-style design. Its sleek color and futuristic aesthetic is perfect for anyone wanting to be different. A lightweight walker for an easy push and storage. The aluminum rollator features a lightweight, durable, and dependable build making it easy for those with weak strength. Easy-to-use side-folding design. Easily store the folding walker in tight spaces, including closets and car trunks. The engineered easy to fold design makes storage quick and painless. Height adjustable 34" to 38". Having the wrong height for a rollator can cause injuries. The aluminum rollator can be height adjusted and is perfect for those up to 6'4" tall. Locking brakes for use when seating. The added safety of locking brakes means you won't have to worry about the mobility walker rolling while seated. Large 8" front wheels for superior maneuverability. The extra-large eight-inch front wheels mean a smooth glide both indoor and outdoor on multiple surfaces. 300 lb. weight capacity. The rollator with seat is a durable and dependable aluminum rollator ideal for those in need of something to use daily. NOTE: Rollators ARE NOT intended to be used as transportation devices. If you're in need of a transportation aid, we advise using a wheelchair or transport chair for maximum safety. Trust in Carex for all your mobility aid needs. For over 35 years, we've been the leader in mobility aids, including rolling walkers. Our wide selection, satisfaction guarantee, and product warranty mean you're well covered with your mobility aid purchase. All of our products are designed to improve, enable, and keep our customers independent. If you're not happy, we'll make it right. Need help selecting the right mobility aid? Read our Mobility Aid Buyer's Guide. We'll cover the many forms of mobility aids, the pros and cons of each, and how to make the right decision. WARNING: This product can expose you to chemicals including Bisphenol A (BPA), which is known to the State of California to cause birth defects or other reproductive harm. For more information, visit www.P65Warnings.ca.gov. Where To Buy Wheel Size: 8" Seat: Padded Backrest: Padded Brakes: Yes Storage Bag: Yes Product Weight: 14 lbs Weight Capacity: 300 lbs.
